text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Quebec Premier to promote secession: Trade mission will be opportunity to talk of Quebec independence, Deputy Premier says.
- Former submarine commander ends hunger strike: Navy restores his former rank.
- Need for intervention force fading: Canadian commander hopeful Zairian crisis will not require troops, airdrops.
- Tobacco ad curbs set out: Cigarette taxes go up today.
- Air carrier, unions at impasse: CAW-CUPE stand upsets some Canadian Airlines workers.
- Follow-up care alarms heart MDs: Specialists say too few patients, particularly women, receive rehabilitation.
- Market's flight expected to continue into '97, barring a major interest rate rise or economic slump.
- RBC's profit a record: Investment dealer tops $154 million.
- Altamira boss alleged to have paid himself $7-million.
- IPL Energy wins battle for utility: Consumers' Gas holders vote to sell.
- Inco picks $1 billion smelter site: Argentia-Long Harbour region gets the nod for Voisey's Bay nickel refinery complex, slated for completion by 2000.
- Canadian pushes ahead with rescue plan.
